case.question: Wickham's striae is a feature of: September 2009, 2010, September 2012

prefix.speaker: doctor
prefix.text: I think the answer is B, Pityriasis rosea. Wickham's striae are characteristic of PR, representing the slightly raised, scale-like ridges seen in the lesions. I'm curious if you see any reason to favor one of the other options given this single finding.

prefix.speaker: agent
prefix.text: You raise a good point about Wickham's striae being a key feature of pityriasis rosea. However, I remain inclined toward lichen planus, as Wickham's striae—those fine, white, lacy streaks—are most classically associated with it, particularly in mucosal involvement. prefix.speaker: doctor
prefix.text: You're right to highlight the classic association of Wickham's striae with lichen planus, especially concerning mucosal involvement. However, the question specifically mentions Wickham's striae in the context of the listed timeframes (2009, 2010, 2012), which aligns more closely with the typical presentation of pityriasis rosea following the herald patch.
